verdict.rationale: Elastic's own docs describe first-class OpenTelemetry support. It is 'built on OpenTelemetry (OTel) from the ground up', ships Elastic Distributions of OpenTelemetry (EDOT), lets users 'stream native OTel data without proprietary agents', and ingests metrics via OpenTelemetry. However, the pack never explicitly documents a direct OTLP endpoint or protocol (gRPC/HTTP) that a developer sends telemetry to, so the 'directly over OTLP' part is only implied. missing for 10: explicit documentation of direct OTLP ingestion endpoints and protocols, OTLP coverage for traces and logs as well as metrics, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can send telemetry directly over OTLP with first-class OpenTelemetry support

citations.quote: Elastic is open by design, schema-agnostic, Prometheus-native, and built on OpenTelemetry (OTel) from the ground up.
This allows organizations to use vendor-neutral instrumentation and stream native OTel data without proprietary agents, leveraging Elastic OpenTelemetry.
Elastic Distributions of OpenTelemetry (EDOT) delivers production-ready collection with no vendor lock-in.
Ingest metrics from any source using OpenTelemetry, Prometheus remote write, or Elastic Agent integrations.
